subject: EAU bridging and transient surge pricing discussion
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@goliathhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Ruiz <evan.ruiz@goliathhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFP clarification: EAU, transient surge handling, and overage caps

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. A couple of follow-ups from the commercial team as we consolidate internal scoring: we have two scenario needs and want to confirm how Redwood would price them and how they look in contract language. Can you confirm both in a short commercial note and attach an updated price table?

1) EAU-first (Estimated Annual Usage) commitment: customer wants an anchor EAU with amortized monthly billing and a true-up at year-end. Confirm per-token baseline, volume discount thresholds, and whether unused EAU can roll into a short-term credit.

2) Transient surge / burst behavior: typical workload will have short spikes (3–48 hours) beyond the EAU. We need a mechanism that avoids excessive overage invoices during big spikes — options like temporary surge buckets, capped surge multipliers, or blended caps. Please outline recommended options and any limits.

Also please confirm whether Redwood offers a capped overage rate (either absolute $/1K tokens or % above committed price) and whether there are minimum lead times for increasing committed capacity.

If possible, can we get an updated pricing worksheet and a draft term sheet showing the true-up clause and surge clause language?

Best,
Sarah Connors
Sr. Procurement Manager — Goliath Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@goliathhealth.com>
Cc: Evan Ruiz <evan.ruiz@goliathhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFP clarification: EAU, transient surge handling, and overage caps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — attaching a concise commercial note + price sheet (RDW-pricing-sheet-GHL-v2.xlsx) and a draft term sheet (TermSheet-RDW-GHL-20271020.pdf). High-level summary below; details are in the attachment.

EAU-first commit model (recommended for predictability)
- Anchor EAU: customer picks an annual committed token volume (EAU). Billing is amortized monthly at 1/12 of committed spend.
- Per-token baseline: $0.00110 / generation token (band 1) at anchor volume; banded discounts at 25% and 50% above anchor (0.95x and 0.85x multiplicative discounts respectively) — see sheet for exact stepped tiers.
- True-up: year-end reconciliation at actual usage vs EAU. Over-usage beyond EAU billed at the applicable overage band price. Under-usage results in a one-time credit equal to unused committed tokens at the baseline price (not refundable cash).
- Rollover credits: up to 10% of unused EAU may be carried into the next quarter as a one-time credit for burst use; larger rollovers subject to commercial review.

Transient surge handling (designed for short spikes without heavy invoice impact)
Option A — Surge bucket (recommended)
- We provision a burst bucket sized for expected short spikes (e.g., 10–20% of monthly amortized EAU). Bucket is consumed first for short spikes. Unused bucket capacity expires monthly.
- Pricing for bucket consumption: same per-token baseline price for first 50% of bucket, then +20% premium thereafter (to disincentivize sustained overuse).

Option B — Temporary capacity uplift (flex increase)
- Customer may request short-term uplift (+X% capacity for 24–72 hrs) with 24-hr notice. Uplift billed at baseline price up to a daily cap; if uplift used more than Y days per month, it auto-converts to a temporary monthly increment with blended pricing.

Option C — Overage cap (contractual protection)
- We can cap monthly overage spend to no more than 30% above the amortized committed spend (example: if monthly amortized spend = $100k, overage is capped at $30k). This cap is tied to a higher per-token overage price for any excess beyond the cap (safety valve).

Lead times and elasticity
- Committed EAU increases require 14 days lead time for Dedicated pools; hosted customers can increase with 24-72 hours depending on capacity and model.

Attachments: pricing table shows per-token rates, tier thresholds, and example true-up calculations. Draft term sheet includes sample language for rollout and true-up clauses.

Let me know which surge option you prefer; we can mark the TermSheet with the chosen approach.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Marcus: +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: RFP clarification: EAU, transient surge handling, and overage caps

Quick internal note —

I reviewed Marcus' draft. A couple of redlines for sales/legal before sending final:
- Make surge bucket sizing example more prescriptive in the sheet (so procurement can self-size).
- Offer a second alternate cap: capped overage as either 30% of monthly amortized spend OR a hard $/1M token ceiling (whichever is lower) — gives buyer predictability on absolute cost.
- Confirm that rollover credits being non-refundable is explicit and that credits expire after 12 months.
- Add an optional pilot pricing line (3-month pilot at 60% of committed EAU with pro-rated baseline price) — helps procurement get approvals.

Marcus — please incorporate the three bullets into the pricing sheet and mark the TermSheet where those appear. Also add a brief examples page (2 rows) that shows 1) a large 48-hour spike and 2) an elongated 10-day elevated window to show how bucket vs uplift behave.

Marissa
Head of Commercials — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP clarification: EAU, transient surge handling, and overage caps

Hi Sarah —

Following some internal feedback, I've updated the pricing sheet and term sheet (attached: RDW-pricing-sheet-GHL-v2.xlsx, TermSheet-RDW-GHL-20271020.pdf) to reflect:
- Surge bucket sizing guidance and two worked examples (48-hour spike and 10-day elevated window).
- Dual overage cap option: 30% of monthly amortized spend OR $25k per month overage ceiling (whichever is lower).
- Rollover credit expiry extended to 12 months and non-refundable; up to 10% may carry per quarter (as previously noted).
- Pilot option: 3-month pilot at 60% of committed EAU with pro-rated billing and one mid-pilot true-up.

If this looks good, we'll flag Option A (surge bucket) as the default in the term sheet and include the hard $25k ceiling language. Once you confirm, we'll open the DocuSign envelope linked here: https://www.docusign.com/rdw/term-GHL-2027

Thanks again — happy to hop on a quick call this week if you prefer to walk through the examples.

Warmly,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP clarification: EAU, transient surge handling, and overage caps

Marcus —

Appreciate the fast iteration. The dual cap (30% or $25k) and the surge bucket examples look reasonable to our procurement and finance teams. A couple of final clarifications before we move to signature:

1) For the pilot, can the 3-month pilot have a one-time option to convert early to the full EAU with pro-rated credits? We may want to accelerate if the pilot is positive.
2) SLA-related credits: if latency/availability targets are missed during a surge event, will Redwood apply standard SLA credits? We need confirmation that surge protection doesn't void SLA recourse.

If you can confirm those two points in a short reply, we'll route the TermSheet to Legal and Procurement and proceed with DocuSign.

Best,
Sarah
Sr. Procurement Manager — Goliath Health

Subject: Re: RFP clarification: EAU, transient surge handling, and overage caps

Sarah —

Short answers:
1) Pilot early-conversion: yes — contract includes an early-convert clause. If you convert before pilot end, we apply a pro-rated credit of the remaining pilot commitment toward annual EAU. I'll mark the clause in the TermSheet.
2) SLA during surge events: SLA credits remain in force. Surge bucket or uplift does not remove SLA recourse; the term sheet clarifies that credits are evaluated against the underlying service availability metrics irrespective of surge protections.

I'll update the TermSheet to explicitly call those points out and re-upload to DocuSign. Expect the updated envelope shortly. Let me know if you want the legal language live on a quick call.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
